questions.prompt: ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot are examples of…
questions.explanation: They are AI assistants. You ask in normal words, and they write an answer.

questions.prompt: How does an AI chatbot make its answer?
options: It guesses the next words, one by one
It picks it from a fixed list
questions.explanation: It learned from a huge amount of text and guesses the next words. So it can sound right and still be wrong.

questions.prompt: The AI answer sounds very sure. What is true?
options: It comes from a real document
questions.explanation: AI can invent facts that sound real. This is called a “hallucination”.

questions.prompt: AI gives you a number for a client. What do you do first?
options: Ask the AI if it is sure
Check it in a trusted source
Use it if it looks right
questions.explanation: Asking the AI “are you sure?” is not a check. Check numbers, names and laws in the real source.

questions.prompt: Which is OK to paste into a free public AI tool?
questions.explanation: Free public tools may keep what you type. Never paste private client or company data.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use AI with company documents?
options: Use the AI tool the company approved
Send them to a friend who knows AI
questions.explanation: Approved tools have the right security settings. Personal accounts are outside the company's control.

questions.prompt: Which request gets the best result from AI?
options: Write a short, friendly ad for a 2-room apartment near the metro
questions.explanation: Say what you want, who it is for, how long, and the tone. Clear requests get better answers.

questions.prompt: Why can AI give old information about recent events?
options: Its knowledge stops at a certain date
questions.explanation: Many AI models only know the world up to a certain date. Without web search, they can miss new events and prices.

questions.prompt: Which task is AI usually good at?
options: Writing a first draft of an email
questions.explanation: AI is great for drafts, summaries and ideas. A person still checks, decides and signs.

questions.prompt: AI wrote an email with a mistake, and you sent it. Who is responsible?
questions.explanation: If you send it, you own it. Always read AI text before you use it.

questions.prompt: What can many AI tools understand today?
questions.explanation: Many tools can read a photo of a floor plan, a PDF or a table, in many languages.

questions.prompt: The first AI answer is not good enough. What is the best next step?
options: Tell it what to change and try again
questions.explanation: Working with AI is a conversation. Add details, give an example, or ask for changes.

questions.prompt: A voice message from your “boss” asks you to send money now. What do you do?
options: Call your boss on a number you know
questions.explanation: AI can copy voices and faces. Check unusual requests another way before you act.

questions.prompt: What can an AI “agent” do that a simple chatbot cannot?
questions.explanation: An agent can do tasks for you: send, book, update. That is why its access needs care.

questions.prompt: AI learned from human writing. What can it copy from people?
questions.explanation: AI can repeat unfair ideas from its data. Watch for unfair answers about people.
